items.title: Jay-Z Brings His ‘Jay-Z 30’ Concert Series to a Close in Los Angeles With Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg and Too Short
items.summary:
Jay-Z closed his yearlong Jay-Z 30 concert series Saturday night at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, the second of two shows there, with guest turns from Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg and Too $hort. The series began in late May with a one-off headlining set at the Roots Picnic in Philadelphia and grew into a global run after nearly a decade without a new album.

The Los Angeles finale ran about 90 minutes and moved through the catalog era by era, with the familiar segues intact — "Girls, Girls, Girls" into "'03 Bonnie & Clyde," "N—s in Paris" folded into "Big Pimpin'." Too $hort came out for "Blow the Whistle," and Dre and Snoop ran a medley that included "Nuthin' but a 'G' Thang," "Still D.R.E.," "The Next Episode" and "California Love." The guest list was leaner than at earlier stops, where he brought out Jazmine Sullivan, Bilal, Freeway, Beanie Sigel and Peedi Crakk in Philadelphia, and Alicia Keys, Fat Joe and Jadakiss across three nights at Yankee Stadium.

During "Encore," Jay-Z addressed social media claims that SoFi had not sold out and that tickets were given away. "People will tell you that nobody was in here tonight, but you got eyes. You can see," he said, per Variety's account of the show. "This world with AI and everything, it's been going on forever. They called it propaganda before. But now, the technology has caught up and people are tricked."

The framing of the whole series has been legacy — a rapper with a decade-long gap between albums revisiting a catalog of number-one records for an audience that largely watched him build it in real time. The setlist opened with "The Watcher 2" and worked through "Izzo (H.O.V.A.)," "Hard Knock Life (Ghetto Anthem)," "99 Problems," "Empire State of Mind" and "Public Service Announcement" before the close.

Near the end, he rapped the line from "Heart of the City (Ain't No Love)" that doubled as the thesis of the run: "Jigga held you down 30 summers, damn, where's the love?" What follows remains unsettled — collaborators have floated and then walked back talk of a new album, and a Super Bowl Halftime Show has been the subject of speculation without confirmation.

items.title: Jessica Biel Teases How She Plans To “Modernize” ‘7th Heaven’ With Reboot & Create “Safe Space” On Set As EP
items.summary:
Jessica Biel is executive producing a reboot of 7th Heaven at CBS Studios through her Iron Ocean banner, and she has begun describing how she intends to update the Aaron Spelling family drama she grew up on. Biel played Mary Camden across the original series, which ran 11 seasons from 1996 to 2007 on The WB and later The CW.

Speaking on Collider Ladies Night, in comments reported by Deadline, Biel said the new version will take on subjects the original only glanced at. "Technology-based issues, school stuff, bullying stuff, drugs, alcohol," she said. "All of those things we want to address in a very real way, which is, I think, what the original kind of gently touched on, but we were very careful about what our audience wanted. We had a lot of limitations. We have less limitations now."

She also said the show will keep its original shape as something families watch together. "We still want to keep the DNA of what it was, where you can sit down and watch with your families, but we're not going to hold back, I think, as much as we did before," Biel said.

Asked why she is producing rather than returning as Mary, Biel pointed to what she sees as the job of a producer on emotionally demanding material. "It's people really putting themselves out there on the chopping block emotionally, and if you don't have that space protected, I think it's hard," she said, adding that she is "constantly trying" to "build out that space where everyone feels like they will be taken care of, and it's safe."

The original followed Reverend Eric Camden, played by Stephen Collins, his wife Annie (Catherine Hicks) and their children, played by Barry Watson, Biel, Beverley Mitchell, David Gallagher and Mackenzie Rosman. Most of the cast has distanced itself from Collins, who acknowledged in 2014 that he had sexually assaulted three underage girls; he was never charged. No casting, network or premiere timing has been announced for the reboot.

items.title: SAG-AFTRA Votes To Extend Duncan Crabtree-Ireland’s Contract With Updated Title
items.summary:
The SAG-AFTRA National Board voted Saturday to extend National Executive Director Duncan Crabtree-Ireland's contract through June 20, 2032, and to add CEO to his title. The agreement passed with 98.34% of the board in favor, pushing his tenure four years past the June 21, 2028 expiration of his current deal.

The union said the new title better reflects the scope of his work, which includes his continuing role as the guild's chief negotiator. Terms of the agreement were not disclosed, according to Deadline.

"Leading SAG-AFTRA's staff is the honor of my career, and I'm grateful for the opportunity to keep doing this work," Crabtree-Ireland said in a statement. "I intend to fight alongside our leadership to make sure our members control their image, likeness, voice, and destiny in the workplace, and that they are compensated fairly in the process."

SAG-AFTRA President Sean Astin framed the extension as a matter of matching the other side of the table. "To battle giant global transnational corporations, we need expert leadership with a track record of successful bargaining and significant operational management expertise," Astin said. "That is Duncan."

The vote follows the four-year agreement Crabtree-Ireland negotiated with the AMPTP in May. It also lands while the union's leadership is publicly opposing the Paramount Skydance acquisition of Warner Bros., a fight that will now sit with the same negotiator for at least the next six years.
